speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your specific symptoms regarding the gait and limb ataxia you mentioned, and tell me what your significant medical history entails.

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description. Is this ataxia constant, or does it worsen significantly when you look down at your feet or extend your arms? Additionally, have you experienced any recent changes in vision, difficulty swallowing, or slurred speech?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy. Given your history of Crohn's disease and one year of natalizumab use, the onset of ataxia is highly suggestive of this opportunistic infection affecting the white matter of your brain. I need to confirm the extent of brain involvement; REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain with and without contrast.
